forces.title: AI infrastructure boom drives demand for tech hardware
forces.description: The unprecedented surge in AI development and data center build-outs is creating immense demand for advanced semiconductors, which are critical inputs for Technology Hardware & Equipment. Hyperscalers' significant capital expenditures for AI infrastructure are boosting average selling prices and driving sustained growth for leading-edge chips and high-bandwidth memory, directly benefiting manufacturers of servers, storage, networking equipment, and electronic components within IG0803.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Global supply chains de-risk from China, benefiting India's EMS
forces.description: Geopolitical tensions, trade frictions, and lessons from COVID-19 have prompted global OEMs to pivot from China-centric supply chains. There's a new focus on resilience through geographic diversification and multi-node manufacturing networks. This structural shift positions India's Electronic System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) sector (IN080304) as a strategic alternative hub, attracting relocation volumes and fostering significant growth in contract electronics manufacturing.

forces.title: Government PLI schemes catalyze domestic electronics manufacturing
forces.description: India's Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes for large-scale electronics, IT hardware, and electronic components (LSEM, PLI 2.0 for IT Hardware, ECMS, ISM 2.0) are providing substantial fiscal incentives. These policies are the primary catalyst attracting both domestic and global players to scale manufacturing operations in India, boosting local production, attracting investments, and generating jobs across the Technology Hardware & Equipment value chain.

forces.title: Expanding connected devices and electrification drive electronics demand
forces.description: The proliferation of connected devices, from smartphones and IoT systems to the increasing electrification of industries like automotive and manufacturing, is a major demand driver. This trend fuels the need for expanded electronics manufacturing capacity (IN080304) and a wider range of electronic components and systems (IN080306), ensuring sustained demand for various hardware segments within IG0803.

forces.title: Increased OEM outsourcing supports EMS market growth
forces.description: As electronics products become more complex with accelerating production cycles, Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) are increasingly outsourcing manufacturing to Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) providers. This strategy allows OEMs to maintain flexibility and reduce capital investment, leading to a direct benefit and growth opportunity for IN080304 (Electronics System Design & Manufacturing) as these companies become strategic supply chain partners.

forces.title: India's EMS transitioning to higher-value design integration
forces.description: While India's EMS sector is currently concentrated in mobile assembly and basic PCB/box-build, there's a clear evolution towards higher-complexity segments like automotive, industrial, and telecom infrastructure. This strategic upgrade from pure assembly to design integration, requiring engineering depth and sophisticated supply chain management, represents a structural shift for IN080304, moving up the value curve for improved margins.

forces.title: Persistent semiconductor supply-demand imbalance constrains hardware production
forces.description: Despite surging demand, the supply of leading-edge chips and high-bandwidth memory remains limited, creating an ongoing supply-demand imbalance expected to persist for several years. This shortage translates into higher average selling prices and potential production constraints for downstream Technology Hardware & Equipment manufacturers (IG0803), impacting their costs, delivery timelines, and ability to meet demand across various product segments.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: India's EMS faces 'scale without depth' challenge, requiring localization
forces.description: India's rapid growth in EMS has been primarily driven by scale, particularly in mobile assembly, but it risks a 'scale without depth' paradox due to historical focus on services and ecosystem immaturity. High reliance on imported components exposes manufacturers to forex risks, import duties, and supply volatility, necessitating greater localization and backward integration to achieve sustainable growth and mitigate these structural vulnerabilities within IN080304.

forces.title: High electronics import bill reflects component reliance, stifles domestic value-add
forces.description: India's electronics import bill reached a record US$116.17 billion in FY26, a significant increase year-over-year. This high import dependency, particularly for components and modules, highlights a structural vulnerability for the domestic Technology Hardware & Equipment sector. It indicates a 'scale without depth' issue, limiting indigenous value addition and making the industry susceptible to global supply chain disruptions and currency fluctuations.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Major investments boost India's semiconductor and component ecosystem
forces.description: Significant investments are flowing into India's semiconductor and electronic component ecosystem, including Tata Electronics' collaboration with Intel for manufacturing, Syrma SGS Technology's large PCB/CCL facility, and AMD's biggest design facility in India. These initiatives, alongside government support like the expanded ECMS and ISM 2.0, are crucial for strengthening domestic supply chains and reducing import dependency for IN080306 and IN080304.

forces.title: Digital infrastructure investments fuel enterprise hardware demand
forces.description: India is witnessing massive investments in digital infrastructure, with approximately US$70 billion already in progress and a further US$90 billion announced. This, coupled with a tax holiday for foreign companies delivering cloud services from India, is driving a boom in data center expansion and AI adoption. This directly translates into robust demand for Computer Hardware & Enterprise Devices (IN080302) like servers, storage, and networking equipment.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: India emerges as leading smartphone exporter, boosting electronics manufacturing
forces.description: In Q2 FY26, India overtook China to become the top smartphone exporter to the United States, a significant milestone. This achievement, driven by expanded domestic manufacturing capacity, signals India's growing competitiveness in Consumer Electronics & Devices (IN080301) and provides a strong tailwind for the Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (IN080304) sector through increased export orders and global market share.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

viewpoints.title: AI fuels semiconductor surge, pushing value and growth for tech hardware
viewpoints.description: McKinsey's Semiconductors Practice projects unprecedented and sustained growth for the semiconductor industry, driven by AI. This surge leads to significantly higher average selling prices (ASPs) for leading-edge chips and memory. For the Technology Hardware & Equipment sector (IG0803), this translates into a robust tailwind of strong demand and increased value for critical components used in computing, communications, and consumer devices, fostering overall industry expansion and reshaping long-standing growth patterns.
viewpoints.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

viewpoints.title: India's EMS sector poised for significant growth amidst global supply chain shift
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights a positive outlook for India's Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) industry, positioning it as a pivotal alternative manufacturing hub. This growth is propelled by global Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) de-risking their China-centric supply chains due to geopolitical tensions, emphasizing resilience, and actively supported by government initiatives like India's Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes. This creates a strategic opportunity for contract electronics manufacturing and design services (IN080304) to expand significantly.

viewpoints.title: India's electronics manufacturing targets ambitious growth with strong policy support
viewpoints.description: IBEF presents a highly positive outlook for India's Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) sector, aiming for a fivefold increase in manufacturing output to US$500 billion by FY30. This ambitious growth is underpinned by supportive government policies such as the PLI schemes and the India Semiconductor Mission 2.0, coupled with robust domestic demand and rising exports of products like smartphones. The strong policy push is attracting significant investments and driving the expansion of production capacities across the hardware ecosystem.

demand_drivers.description: Proliferation of smartphones, laptops, and IoT-enabled industrial systems drives demand for electronics manufacturing capacity.
Increasing electrification of industries such as automotive, energy, and manufacturing expands demand for electronic components and systems.
OEMs are increasingly outsourcing manufacturing to EMS providers to maintain flexibility and reduce capital investment due to product complexity and accelerated production cycles.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated global EMS market size in 2025. Projections indicate continued expansion to over USD 1 trillion by early 2030s at a CAGR of roughly 6.5-7%. Covers consumer electronics, computing hardware, telecommunications infrastructure, and automotive electronics.

demand_drivers.description: Growing internal consumption of electronic products in India, driven by rising disposable incomes and digitalization.
Increasing exports of electronic goods from India, particularly mobile phones.
OEMs' increasing reliance on EMS providers for manufacturing.

market_sizing.methodology: India's EMS market expanded from USD 10-12 billion in FY20 to USD 40-45 billion in FY25. Projected to cross USD 150 billion by FY30, growing at >25% CAGR. India's share of global EMS manufacturing remains modest at 5-6%.

demand_drivers.description: General market demand for electronic products and systems.
Government initiatives and schemes promoting the ESDM sector.
Rising adoption of digital technologies across various sectors.

market_sizing.methodology: Indian electronics system design and manufacturing (ESDM) market valued at US$ 90 billion in FY19, estimated to reach US$ 220 billion by FY25, growing at a CAGR of 16.1%. Includes IT, office automation, telecom, consumer electronics, aviation, aerospace, defence, solar photovoltaic, nano electronics, and medical electronics hardware products/components, and design activities like product, chip, VLSI, board, and embedded systems.
India's electronics industry is targeting a manufacturing output of US$ 500 billion by FY30, which requires a fivefold increase in production.

India IT Hardware market reached US$ 22.61 billion in 2026, growing from US$ 21.17 billion in 2025. It is expected to reach US$ 31.39 billion in 2031 at a CAGR of 6.78%. The domestic market accounts for a significant share.
market_sizing.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

market_sizing.methodology: India’s appliance and consumer electronics market is expected to become the fourth-largest globally by FY27, with revenues projected at Rs. 3,00,000 crore (US$ 31.79 billion) by FY29.

demand_drivers.description: Rapid build-out and upgrades of data centers globally, requiring new server capacity.
Increased investment in AI technologies drives demand for high-performance servers and related infrastructure.

market_sizing.methodology: Global server expenditure is anticipated to surge by 36.9% year-on-year in 2026. This reflects strong demand for enterprise IT hardware (IN080302) driven by data center expansion and AI.
market_sizing.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: Hyperscalers and enterprises are investing heavily in AI-driven data centers, demanding significant hardware.
Expansion of cloud compute, storage, and networking services requires continuous data center infrastructure upgrades.

market_sizing.methodology: Overall global data center spending is projected to climb 31.7%, exceeding US$ 650 billion in 2026, compared with almost US$ 500 billion the prior year. This spending drives demand for computer hardware and networking equipment (IN080302, IN080303).
market_sizing.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India
